identity.name: SHREE DIGVIJAY CEM CO LTD
identity.industry: Gujarat Regional Cement & Oil Well Specialty Materials

summary.oneLiner: Shree Digvijay has executed a strategic Brand Usage & Distribution Agreement (BDA) with Hi-Bond Cement, instantly scaling combined capacity to 5.2 MTPA and securing ~10% Gujarat market share without immediate capex burden. While Q4FY26 benefits from a INR 25-30/bag price hike and stable costs, FY27 margins face a structural ~INR 200/ton compression due to increased reliance on purchased clinker to feed new grinding capacity, partially offset by high-margin oil well cement (15% of revenue).

one-line thesis: Shree Digvijay has executed a strategic Brand Usage & Distribution Agreement (BDA) with Hi-Bond Cement, instantly scaling combined capacity to 5.2 MTPA and securing ~10% Gujarat market share without immediate capex burden. While Q4FY26 benefits from a INR 25-30/bag price hike and stable costs, FY27 margins face a structural ~INR 200/ton compression due to increased reliance on purchased clinker to feed new grinding capacity, partially offset by high-margin oil well cement (15% of revenue).
financial scorecard: Revenue: Guided up 8-10% YoY in Q4 on volume + price; EBITDA/margin: Q4 stable, but FY27 EBITDA/ton expected to dip ~INR 200 due to clinker outsourcing; PAT: Not disclosed, linked to volume ramp; Order book: N/A (commodity); Net debt: Rose to INR 485 Cr (INR 132 Cr existing + INR 356 Cr new loan for BDA), interest rate 8.7%.
guidance: Revenue growth: 8-10% YoY in Q4; double-digit volume growth expected FY27; Margin: Q4 stable, FY27 pressure from clinker costs offset by product mix; Order inflow: N/A; Capex/commissioning: 1.5 MTPA grinding unit commissioned Oct 2025, no new capex planned until 70-75% utilization reached.
order book & pipeline: N/A - Commodity business; Sales volume guided at 3.0-3.5 MTPA for FY27 (combined entity).
segment / subsidiary detail: Core Cement (OPC/PPC/Slag): 85% of volume, focused on Saurashtra/Gujarat; Oil Well Cement: 7-8% volume but 15% revenue contribution, 90% market share in India among oil well players; Hi-Bond Integration: Adds 2.2 MTPA grinding capacity, currently operating at ~1 MTPA.
growth verticals / optionality: Market share expansion in Gujarat from 10% to 14-15%; Potential exercise of call option on Hi-Bond assets post-milestone alignment; Captive jetty commercialization (discussions with Reliance/TPS for 1-1.5 MTPA cargo, not yet confirmed); Limestone mine acquisitions (20 MTPA recently acquired, 600 MTPA reserve in vicinity).
margins & cost dynamics: Q4FY26: Net price increase INR 25-30/bag, no cost inflation expected; FY27 Outlook: EBITDA/ton compression of ~INR 200 due to purchased clinker (clinker factor ~55%); Hi-Bond contribution: Expected INR 200-300/ton EBITDA after paying cost-plus-INR 500 fee; Fuel risk: Brent crude/petcoke rise to be passed through to customers.
capex / expansion: Recent: 1.5 MTPA grinding unit commissioned Oct 2025; Future: No immediate clinkerization capex; Plan to explore limestone mines and potential clinker plant only after reaching 70-75% utilization of current 5.2 MTPA capacity.
capital allocation: Debt-funded growth: INR 356 Cr raised for BDA transaction; Deleveraging: Repaying INR 24-25 Cr annually; Promoter stance: Long-term view by IRF (Piramal/Bain), professional management run.
risks & watch-items: Margin dilution from high clinker procurement costs; Geopolitical supply chain disruptions affecting clinker/coal imports; Delay in commercializing captive jetty; Execution risk in integrating Hi-Bond operations; Dependence on Gujarat/Saurashtra regional demand.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes volume growth over immediate margin expansion; Transparent about clinker cost headwinds but confident in pass-through mechanisms; Professional and process-driven regarding potential Hi-Bond acquisition.
non-obvious takeaways: Oil Well Cement division commands ~90% share of Indian oil well cement market (ONGC, Oil India, Schlumberger) contributing disproportionately to revenue (15%) vs volume (7-8%); Hi-Bond plant has captive power meeting 80% needs, making its base production cost lower than Digvijay's, creating an arbitrage even after the INR 500/ton fee.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Regional cement prices under pressure from oversupply; high fuel costs | UltraTech Cement | beneficiary | Med | As the market leader, UltraTech benefits from any regional price stabilization in Gujarat triggered by Digvijay/Hi-Bond's disciplined pricing and capacity rationalization. |
| Rising clinker costs and supply chain disruptions | Small regional grinders without captive power or jetty access | loser | High | Competitors lacking Digvijay's captive jetty for imports or Hi-Bond's captive power will face higher cost bases and inability to pass on costs as effectively. |

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.
